newsitem.title: CANADA: Vancouver's port opens new container terminal.
newsitem.headline: Vancouver's port opens new container terminal.

text.p: The Port of Vancouver opened a new C$224 million container terminal Wednesday that doubles its container handling capacity.

About 40 km south of Vancouver, the facility called Deltaport will be capable of handling about one million teu (20-foot equivalent units) a year. The city's other terminals have already reached capacity.
The project was funded by the Vancouver Port Corp, TSI Terminal Systems Inc and the Canadian National and Canadian Pacific railways.
Deltaport features an on-dock intermodal facility with direct access to what it said were the only two transcontinental rail lines in North America, Canadian National and Canadian Pacific.
The facility has two container berths able to handle the biggest ships in the world and high-tech gantries capable of loaing two double-stacked trains simultaneously.
The terminal is designed to meet Vancouver's projected growth in container traffic over the next 10 years.
